knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The lesson says chemical containers must not go in general waste, and each stream has its own route set by the site, council and state rules. The designated chemical waste route is therefore correct. General waste (option 0) and unrinsed recycling (option 2) are not valid routes.

Wash water discharge depends on location rules that must be checked first; where no route is approved, the water is collected and referred. Discharging straight away (option 0) and pouring it onto a garden (option 2) skip that check.
The lesson says that in many places discharge to a stormwater drain is not allowed, and discharge to a sewer may need approval.

practicalCriteria: Learner sorts a supplied set of waste items into the correct streams at the point of generation.
Learner identifies which items must not go in general waste, including sharps, chemical containers and liquids.
Learner states the discharge check required before wash water goes to any drain, and collects the water where no approved route exists.
Learner records a specialist or hazardous waste item with its quantity and route.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Waste record for hazardous or specialist waste, with quantity, route and receiver
Record of any wash water collected and where it was taken
stopWorkCriteria: Learner puts sharps, chemical containers or liquids in general waste
Learner discharges wash water to a drain without confirming the route
Learner takes hazardous waste home or into a customer bin
